previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a 58-year-old male with acute myeloid leukemia in remission following double cord blood transplant, was admitted for evaluation of a painful right lower extremity rash concerning for cellulitis. He presented with erythema, warmth, and inability to bear weight, but no trauma or fever. Initial treatment included IV vancomycin and cefepime. Imaging showed no evidence of osteomyelitis or DVT, and blood cultures remained negative. The rash improved significantly, and he was transitioned to oral clindamycin and ciprofloxacin for completion at home. Acute kidney injury was noted, likely due to medication or dehydration, and managed with temporary discontinuation of lisinopril. His vision concerns were evaluated and attributed to chronic steroid use, with ophthalmology follow-up arranged. He remained stable, completed treatment, and was discharged home with instructions to continue antibiotics, monitor for recurrence, and follow up with specialists.
problems: Cellulitis and abscess of leg, except foot
Peripheral stem cells replaced by transplant
Unspecified hereditary and idiopathic peripheral neuropathy
Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage I through stage IV, or unspecified

linear opacity, possibly due to atelectasis, improved.  Minimal bronchiectasis
is still in the right upper lobe, but bronchial wall thickening improved since
___.

Central venous line was removed.  Multiple mediastinal lymph nodes are still
enlarged but decreased, down to 18 mm in short axis.  Coronary artery
calcifications are still minimal.  There are no signs of volume overload.
Heart size is normal.  Severe anemia is suggested by relative ___ of
the interventricular septum.  Main pulmonary artery is top normal.

This study was not tailored for subdiaphragmatic evaluation except to note
prior cholecystectomy and splenomegaly.  There is no suspicious bone lesion
for malignancy.

IMPRESSION:

1.  New clustered peribronchovascular and peribronchiolar nodules in the right
upper lobe and less marked in the left upper lobe, suggesting endobronchial
spread of infection.

2.  Diffuse heterogeneous attenuation and widespread air trapping is more
marked than on ___, probably related to acute infectious process and
small airway disease.  Rapid progression makes bronchiolitis obliterans very
less likely.

3.  No volume overload.  No pleural effusion.

4.  Splenomegaly and mediastinal and hilar lymphadenopathy.

EXAM:  MRI of the brain.

CLINICAL INFORMATION:  Confusion, memory loss and recent hypoxic respiratory
failure, rule out vascular disease or hypoxic injury.

TECHNIQUE:  T1 sagittal and FLAIR, T2 susceptibility and diffusion axial
images acquired.  3D time-of-flight MRA of the circle of ___ obtained.

FINDINGS BRAIN MRI:

No evidence of acute infarct seen.  In particular, there is no evidence of
abnormal signal in the basal ganglia to indicate global hypoxia.  There is
mild brain atrophy seen.  No evidence of significant subcortical white matter
ischemic disease identified.  There is no midline shift or hydrocephalus.

IMPRESSION:  No evidence of acute infarct or signs of acute or chronic
ischemia.

MRA OF THE HEAD:

The head MRA demonstrates normal flow signal within the arteries of anterior
and posterior circulation.  No evidence of vascular occlusion, stenosis or an
aneurysm greater than 3 mm in size is seen.

IMPRESSION:  Normal MRA of the head.
